description: Every forgotten machine in the vastness of space has a heartbeat, a legacy, and a story waiting to be told. We are The Nebula Narrators, a team of passionate STEM minds on a mission to ignite the Afterlight of humanity’s abandoned cosmic pioneers.
summary: As a team who is participating for the first time on the hackathon, We are from different majors and academic stages so at first, we were searching for a midpoint between us, to communicate and divide the tasks among us before the hackathon starts to make easier during the 48 hours together, first we searched for the challenge that we are going to, and we decided to take the abandoned but not forgotten we recorded everyone in the team skills and we found that the most repeated skill was the storytelling and the web development and we found that this challenge fits us, In addition we were curious about knowing the equipment that were sent to the space and didn't come again and what was its mission, thus we started our plan for the hackathon and we collected some information about the equipment that were sent to the space before NASA's resources to have a brief and started our website, Our target audience are teens from 12 to 16 years old who are enthusiast about the space but do not have the trusted resource to collect from it the information and facts so our aim in our website is to offer a trusted resource and in an easier and funny way to keep the information in their head, by pressing on the planet you will find the equipment there and what was their mission and if it is still working or not and that was the summary for our website
details:
AFTERLIGHT is an interactive educational website that transforms the stories of abandoned NASA exploration equipment on the Moon and Mars into an engaging space adventure. Designed primarily for young learners aged 12–16, it allows visitors to explore a cosmic universe screen and navigate an animated Solar System featuring the Sun, eight planetary orbits, and Earth's Moon.

Users can interact with celestial bodies to explore NASA scientific profiles, or select the Moon and Mars to enter their surface archives. Interactive coordinate grids and glowing star hotspots reveal the locations of abandoned equipment, including Surveyor 3, Apollo 12 ALSEP, Opportunity, and Spirit. Each equipment dossier presents a child-friendly mission summary, authentic NASA photographs, verified hardware subsystems, scientific information, and links to primary NASA sources.

The Apollo 12 ALSEP / Intrepid story also features an interactive voiceover player, allowing visitors to listen to the equipment's story through an engaging first-person narrative.

Our project makes complex scientific information accessible, enjoyable, and memorable through cinematic visuals, animated planetary exploration, interactive maps, storytelling, and audio experiences.

AFTERLIGHT is developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, with SVG-based animations and HTML5 audio. Its content is grounded in NASA's official archives, mission records, and imagery.

What makes AFTERLIGHT unique is its storytelling approach: instead of presenting abandoned equipment as lists of scientific facts, we turn each machine's mission into a story worth discovering. Our intended impact is to inspire curiosity about space exploration, encourage scientific learning, and make NASA's knowledge more accessible to young audiences.
